resources.string: Not enough shows to fight
You need at least two shows you’ve seen. The catch-up finds them in a few taps.

Every duel counts. After each vote, CineSwipe recomputes your whole ranking from all your duels (Bradley-Terry model, a cousin of chess Elo): the order of matches no longer matters, and a win against a highly ranked show weighs more.
Matches are chosen to learn as fast as possible: a new show faces well-placed shows of similar level, like a binary search.
“Tie” if you can’t pick between the two shows, “Skip” if you don’t remember one of them.
Faded stars are provisional: the show hasn’t fought enough yet (three or four duels are usually enough).
Reliability: the average probability that your shows’ stars are right to within half a star. It goes up with every duel; around 90 %, your ranking is solid.

resources.string: TV mode: the shows you’ve seen, where you’re at, picks that feel like you and a ranking built from duels. A world of its own, your movies don’t change a thing.
Swipe left if you’ve seen the show, right to keep it for later (or request it from Seerr or Sonarr, the whole show or a few seasons).
Two shows, you pick your favorite: your TV ranking computes itself, apart from your movies.
Find the shows you’ve seen in a few taps, and say where you’re at: finished, in progress, random episodes or dropped.
A step-by-step tour, in a demo with the 100 most-watched shows and a fake profile that has already seen about twenty. Nothing is saved, and you’ll find it again in the settings.
You’re exploring TV mode with the 100 most-watched shows and a fake profile. Nothing is saved: when you leave, your real data is back.
Welcome to the TV demo

In two minutes, we’ll tour TV mode with a fake profile that has already seen about twenty shows (some finished, others in progress or dropped) and a fake Seerr. Try anything you like: nothing is saved.
One card = one show chosen for you. The purple line under the poster says why: a show you liked, a creator, a great classic… The number of seasons and the episode length are under the title.
The show joins your seen shows (its details page then lets you say where you’re at: finished, in progress with the season, random episodes or dropped). Drag the card to the left.
It joins your watchlist. With Seerr or Sonarr, you then choose to request the whole show or only a few seasons, or just keep it on your watchlist.
The show goes by without changing anything. It may come back later, if your tastes change.
“Not for me” dismisses the show for good, “Trailer” opens the trailer on YouTube, and ⚡ chains picks from this show. Tap the poster to open the details: seasons, progress, current season.
Two shows you’ve seen face off. Tap the one you prefer.
The catch-up scrolls through the shows you’re most likely to have seen. Open it.
One tap: finished. Two: in progress. Three: random episodes (watched here and there, on TV). Four: dropped. A long press also offers “watchlist” or the show’s details.
“Next” saves the page. Shows without an answer become “not seen”, with no effect on your picks. Those put on your watchlist offer their request, season by season.
This button switches to cards, with the same gestures as the picks. The filters at the top target a period or French shows.
Type a title: results come as cards, with the same gestures as the picks. Type a name: actors and creators show up, with all their shows. In the demo, it covers the sandbox’s 100 shows.

Your counters open your TV library (“In progress” filter, and swipe from one details page to the next) or the duel history. Further down: your tastes in numbers, your year in review, your own lists and your Hall of Fame.
The Movies | TV switch, your TMDB key (the same for both), your homelab (Plex, Jellyfin to know where you’re at; Seerr or Sonarr for requests) and the backup of your data.

Keep exploring the demo freely, or leave it to get back to your shows. “Tour”, in the banner, restarts the tour. Outside the demo, the Movies | TV switch at the top of the screens takes you back to movies.

resources.string: Import or restore shows
Your seen shows, their progress, your ratings and watchlist from a CineSwipe TV backup, Trakt, IMDb or a CSV file.

Bring over your seen shows, watchlist and ratings from a CineSwipe backup, Trakt or IMDb. A CineSwipe backup on an empty library is restored in full (progress, duels, ranking); the rest is merged without erasing anything. With Trakt, progress is picked up: finished, or in progress with the season.
In TV mode: Settings › My data › Export my data (cineswipe-series-….json file). On a new phone, the backup is restored in full, duels and ranking included.
These files weren’t recognized. Choose the export of one of the apps below (ZIP, CSV or JSON).
